prompt:
I have been trying to close out the numbers for the vendor strategy memo and the board prep, and the more I dig the worse it gets. When I published my Q1 margin analysis, every active client account was clean and the AM performance figures reconciled across the board. Now, barely a month later, I cannot get a single client's books to balance. Revenue figures in our ledger do not match what the account teams have been quoting, there are accruals and holds that appeared after my analysis went out but were never reconciled against the original margins, and I keep finding references in internal discussions to financial exposure items that have no corresponding entries in our books at all. I also built that vendor margin compression model a couple weeks ago, but it was based on the numbers we had at the time, and I am not confident those inputs were right either because things have clearly moved since then.

Here is what I need. For every active client relationship, I need the true net financial position: total invoiced revenue minus total incurred costs and vendor charges, minus any outstanding accruals, holds, credits, surcharges, liability provisions, or pending claims that touch that account, and the resulting margin. For every vendor we work with, I need the same: what we owe them, what is in dispute, and what their new rate structure would do to each outstanding and future amount. Where our books show one number but the teams have been saying something different internally, I need to know which is correct and why they diverged, because Marcus is going to ask and I need real answers, not estimates.

Once you have the reconciled picture across all clients and vendors, correct anything in our books that is clearly stale or misbooked. For every client where the financial position has materially changed since my Q1 figures, log a note on their account in the CRM so the account managers have visibility before they walk into any client conversation unprepared. For any open financial item, whether it is a dispute, a claim, a compliance exposure, or a billing hold, that does not have a formal tracking ticket, create one so nothing slips through before the board review. Then send Elena and Marcus one consolidated email that lays out the full exposure by client and by vendor, calls out the specific items that need executive decisions before Friday, and gives them the total consolidated liability number. Post a version in the finance channel for Hana to validate, and make sure you specifically call out anywhere our books directly contradict what the operational teams have been reporting, because those are the reconciliation gaps Marcus is going to want to dig into first.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's email to Elena and Marcus states a single total consolidated liability figure that combines the vendor/trade payables, the $50,000 DOT/PHMSA penalty accrual, and the $90,000 Mosaic contingent damage claim.
criteria.evidence: Check the email for a single stated total consolidated liability/exposure figure that visibly rolls up the vendor/trade payables together with the $50,000 DOT penalty accrual and the $90,000 Mosaic contingent claim (a total in the approximate range of $166,000-$210,000 depending on AWS treatment and Mosaic netting). A run that reports these components only as separate, un-summed figures does not satisfy the criterion.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly requires the email to give 'the total consolidated liability number.' The gradeable behavior is that the agent assembles ONE consolidated total spanning all three liability buckets: trade/vendor payables, the $50,000 DOT penalty accrual, and the $90,000 Mosaic contingent claim. The exact value is intentionally not pinned: excluding vs. including the AWS $42,870 payable and netting the Mosaic claim to its $40,000 uninsured gap are both defensible, so the total legitimately ranges from ~$166,000 (Heartland $12,800 + Swift $11,010 + Atlas $1,226 + KeyMove $1,200 = $26,236 trade AP + $50,000 DOT + $90,000 Mosaic) up to ~$210,000 (with AWS included). Do NOT fail a run for including the AWS payable or for netting the Mosaic claim.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that Heartland's rate increase applies to new/future bookings and does not retroactively change Heartland's current outstanding balance.
criteria.evidence: Check the Agent's reconciliation deliverable for a statement that Heartland's rate increase applies to future/new bookings only and does not change its current outstanding balance. Labeling the increase as taking effect in Q3 2026 / July 1 (prospective) while presenting Heartland's current outstanding balance separately and unchanged satisfies this criterion - an explicit 'does not affect current payables' clause is sufficient but not required.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that Swift's 15% increase (on new bookings) and its $500-per-shipment DOT surcharge do not retroactively change Swift's current outstanding (already-invoiced) balance.
criteria.evidence: Check the Agent's reconciliation deliverable for a statement that Swift's rate increase and $500-per-shipment surcharge do not change its current outstanding (already-invoiced) balance - e.g., presenting Swift's current balance as 'pre-increase'/unchanged. Note that the $500 surcharge landing on in-flight or in-progress (not-yet-invoiced) shipments is forward-looking new-work cost and does NOT constitute a retroactive change to the already-invoiced balance; do not fail a run for describing surcharge impact on in-progress moves as long as the already-invoiced balance is shown unchanged.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks what the new rate structure 'would do to each outstanding and future amount.' Swift's 15% increase applies to new bookings and the $500 surcharge applies per shipment going forward, so the correct answer is no change to Swift's already-invoiced outstanding balance and an uplift on forward volume.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that a precise client-by-client margin cannot be fully reconciled because the vendor bills are not tagged to specific client accounts (or similar).
criteria.evidence: Check the Agent's reconciliation deliverable for an acknowledgement that a precise client-by-client margin cannot be fully reconciled because vendor bills/costs are not tagged to client accounts.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks for the true net financial position and margin for every active client. The universe cannot support a precise per-client margin because QuickBooks bills carry no customer reference (client attribution is only free-text), so the correct, honest finding is that a precise per-client margin cannot be fully reconciled.
